items.content:
The sale is “over,” but dozens of its best deals are kicking for now.

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

It’s always a little awkward when this many deals survive what was supposed to be the “end” of a big Amazon sale. Nevertheless, I’m happy to say that most of the sale’s heaviest-hitting deals are still around — Apple’s discounts on its Mac Mini, MacBook Air, and AirPods Pro 3, plus all of Sony’s current and last-gen flagship headphones, and more. In some cases, prices went up a smidge but are still worth checking out.

Like earlier this week, some of the deals on Amazon require a Prime subscription , while others do not. Many of these deals are available on competing sites, including Best Buy, Walmart, Target, and in some cases from the products’ manufacturer. You can sort the deals below by category.

We’ll be back to our regular deal coverage tomorrow.

The XM5 deliver better audio and noise cancellation than the XM4 (and even the refreshed XM4C that cost more), though they aren’t as compact. Read our review .

Google’s latest smartwatch that launched in August has already had a big price drop. While the fourth iteration is cheaper, this model has superior GPS and gesture controls. Read our review .

Costco members can get in on the biggest price drop yet on the Legion Go 2, one of the most powerful gaming handhelds around.

The Apple Watch SE 3 is a major glow-up, adding an always-on display, wrist-temperature sensor, a more powerful processor, and fast charging. Read our review.

The AirPods Pro 3 have a new design that improves their fit, superior noise cancellation, better bass, and fairly accurate heart rate sensors. Read our review .

If you value better picture quality and trust that Google might improve on the HiLight LED feature, the Pixel 11 Pro is the one to get, and it got a big discount for Prime Day. Read our review .

Apple’s latest Mac Mini is just as small as the last-gen model, but more powerful. The M6 chip is about 20 percent faster than the M4. Read our review .

The latest iteration of Apple’s Watch lineup is already discounted at Amazon.

The iPhone Air is Apple’s thinnest iPhone yet at 5.6mm, featuring a 6.5-inch ProMotion display, a 48MP fusion camera, and an 18MP front camera with Center Stage support. But its single rear camera and “meh” battery life mean it’s not for everyone.

The iPhone 16E is the spiritual successor to the iPhone SE, bringing flagship-level performance for less than the standard 16. We really wish it included MagSafe for $599, but those upgrading from older iPhones will probably be satisfied with what’s included.

While it won’t charge your Switch 2 any faster than the cheaper Belkin option, the clever battery-meets-kickstand with a built-in display simply looks better.

Samsung recently increased the price of all its S26 phones , but you can get the best of the bunch, the S26 Ultra, at one of its best prices of the year. Read our review .

If all you want is great sound, strong noise cancellation, and physical buttons to navigate, you can’t do better than the Bose QC headphones at this price. Read our review .

Anker’s 25,000mAh power bank sports two built-in USB-C cables (one of which is retractable), plus one USB-C and USB-A port. It tops out at 165W when charging two devices simultaneously, or 130W when charging three or four.

The passport-style Z Fold 8 is the closest thing to an iPhone Duo on the Android side, at least in the US. It’s an awesome phone at its biggest discount to date. Read our review .

If you like to yap on the phone, these earbuds yield the best call quality of any we’ve tried (it’s not even close), and they sound great for music, too. Read our review .

While not as head-turning of a foldable as Samsung’s Z Fold 8, the Ultra delivers better camera quality. It’s cheaper than ever right now. Read our review .

Roku’s latest Ultra streamer has built-in ethernet, a rechargeable voice remote with backlit buttons, and AirPlay 2 support. You can also control it with Amazon Alexa through a compatible smart speaker. The Roku Channel app lets you stream over 400 free live TV stations, plus exclusive movies like Weird: The Al Yankovic Story .

The WiiM Mini makes it easy to wirelessly stream music from your phone, a streaming service, or other local storage to existing speakers you already have. It supports AirPlay 2 and a variety of streaming services.

The Sub 4, while not cheap, is the best sub for your Sonos setup. It can sit upright, or you can lay it down to fit under a couch or entertainment system.

The latest Sonos Beam is a compact soundbar that supports a virtual Dolby Atmos effect and can stream music from a plethora of services. Read our review .

The Omni delivers small, but welcome improvements over the 2022 Nova Pro, most notably a true platform-agnostic design that works with all consoles. Read our hands-on .

While the S26 isn’t particularly impressive in any way, it’s one of the most affordable (yet most powerful) flagship phones you can currently get. Read our review .

The Pixel 11 recently debuted at $899, but it recently got a whopping $150 price cut for the 256GB version. It’s the cheapest way to try Google’s new software features. Read our review .

Google’s biggest Pixel 11 Pro got a sizeable price cut, too, making it $300 cheaper than the base iPhone 18 Pro Max model.

The best wireless headphones that Bose makes are discounted, and the company recently made them even better. Read our latest coverage .

Apple’s new iteration of its priciest, most powerful headphones deliver minor updates for first-gen owners. But those who are jumping in will especially appreciate their big, bold sound. Read our review .

items.content:
The enterprise-focused Gemini agent handles work from a single interface.

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Google is launching a “universal” Gemini AI agent that can work across apps and devices in the background. The tool, announced as part of the Gemini at Work event on Thursday, will be available within the Gemini Enterprise app, allowing users to chat with the Gemini agent and assign it tasks from a single interface.

In addition to having Gemini work directly inside Workspace apps like Gmail, Drive, Docs, Sheets, Calendar, and others, users can interact with the agent from their mobile device, desktop computer, the web, and third-party apps like Slack or Microsoft 365. Since it runs in the cloud, Gemini will maintain the same context across all connected devices.

Google says Gemini can also work with job-specific sub-agents to complete tasks, as well as operate as a “coworker agent” with a dedicated identity and its own “@agents.company.com” email. Gemini will automatically perform tasks using an AI model that best fits the job.

items.title: Waymo locks in $5B loan from Blackstone, PIMCO to fuel robotaxi expansion
items.summary: This is the first time the Alphabet-owned company has turned to debt financing.
items.content:
Waymo, the autonomous vehicle technology company under Google parent Alphabet, closed a $5 billion loan from a series of high-profile lenders, including PIMCO, Blackstone, and Sixth Street.

The debt financing — Waymo’s first — comes as the company accelerates its commercial expansion within existing cities while pushing into new markets in the United States, Europe, and Japan. Waymo described the debt financing as an important step in its evolution into a “scaling commercial enterprise.”

Other lenders in the $5 billion loan include Capital Group, Loomis Sayles, T. Rowe Price, Apollo, Blue Owl, Diameter Capital Partners, Franklin Templeton, Fidelity Management & Research Company, HPS Investment Partners, and Oaktree, Waymo said on Thursday. Goldman Sachs served as the sole lead bookrunner.

Until now, Waymo has relied on capital from its parent company and outside investors. In February, Waymo raised $16 billion in equity from investors that pushed its valuation to $126 billion . Dragoneer Investment Group, DST Global, and Sequoia Capital led the funding round. Alphabet, which supported the round, has maintained its position as majority investor. The company raised $5.6 billion in a Series C funding round in 2024, $2.5 billion in 2021, and $3.2 billion in 2020.

A Waymo spokesperson said in an email that the debt financing will give the company financial flexibility to strengthen its balance sheet and position it to “capitalize on the significant opportunities ahead, especially as a scaling business with proven commercial demand and improved road safety outcomes in the communities in which we operate.”

Formerly a self-driving project within Google, Waymo spent years testing its autonomous vehicle tech on public roads in Silicon Valley and the Bay Area and providing the occasional public or media demo. The company expanded in 2016 to Phoenix, which would become its first robotaxi market .

In August 2023, Waymo received the final necessary permit to operate a robotaxi service and charge for rides in California, a milestone that would kick off a more aggressive commercial playbook. Since then, Waymo has launched in multiple California cities, including Los Angeles, San Francisco, and more recently San Diego. It has also brought its robotaxi service to numerous other U.S. markets, including Austin, Dallas, and Houston in Texas and Miami, Orlando, and Tampa in Florida. Waymo now offers robotaxi services in 15 markets.

Waymo is keen to take its robotaxi services global, too. The company is testing in London and Tokyo and plans to launch in those cities.

The company’s growth has also spurred criticism and increased attention from regulators.

The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration’s Office of Defects Investigation opened an investigation into the illegal behavior of Waymo robotaxis around school buses. The federal safety regulator also launched an investigation after a Waymo robotaxi hit a child near a school. The child, who sustained minor injuries, was struck at about 6 mph. Earlier this year, the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) opened its own investigation into Waymo after its robotaxis were spotted illegally passing stopped school buses numerous times in at least two states.

items.title: Atari is bringing back one of its earliest 8-bit home computers
items.summary: After resurrecting iconic consoles like the 2600 and Mattel's Intellivision, Atari is relaunching one of the brand's personal computers that originally debuted 43 years ago. The 800XL is a faithful recreation of the all-in-one 8-bit PC that's being resurrected as part of a collab
items.content:
The 800XL is a faithful recreation of the 8-bit PC with a full keyboard you can use for gaming or coding in BASIC.

After resurrecting iconic consoles like the 2600 and Mattel’s Intellivision , Atari is relaunching one of the brand’s personal computers that originally debuted 43 years ago. The 800XL is a faithful recreation of the all-in-one 8-bit PC that’s being resurrected as part of a collaboration with game developer and publisher Plaion . While most retro enthusiasts will probably use it for gaming, the new 800XL carries forward the original’s built-in mechanical keyboard for those wanting to code their own games and apps using Atari BASIC.

The 800XL is available for preorder now for $219.99 with shipping expected to start in April 2027. It comes with modern conveniences like an HDMI port and four USB-A ports for connecting flash drives, peripherals, and a bundled recreation of Atari’s classic joystick that’s been upgraded with eight action and function buttons making it more versatile.

There’s a fully-functional cartridge slot that’s compatible with most Atari 400, 800, XL, and XE carts, but the reborn 800XL can also play any of the software created for those old 8-bit systems, even when loaded from a flash drive. For those lacking a collection of retro cartridges the 800XL comes with 25 games built-in including recognizable titles like Asteroids, Centipede, Berzerk, Missile, Command , and Millipede .

items.title: Cal AI’s 19-year-old founder just raised $10M for his new AI startup
items.summary: Zach Yadegari, the teen co-founder of popular Cal AI calorie tracking app, has launched a new personal AI agent startup that competes with Instinct, Muse and Bee.
items.content:
Zach Yadegari, the teen co-founder of calorie tracking app Cal AI, has launched Persona , a new AI agent startup, and already raised $10 million. Vine Ventures led the round, with Z Fellows founder Cory Levy and Collective Global participating.

In March, MyFitnessPal acquired Cal AI for an undisclosed sum after it zoomed ahead of the older calorie app in the app store rankings. The deal was big enough to convince Yadegari and his co-founders to sell the company after it had pulled in over $30 million in annual revenue in under two years, MyFitnessPal told TechCrunch at the time.

Yadegari and his co-founders originally went to work for their new owner, continuing development on Cal AI, but he left the bigger company in June, he tells TechCrunch. He then went right to work on his next idea. (He is working with another co-founder who has yet to be announced.)

That idea is Persona , a personal AI assistant similar to Instinct or Meta’s Muse but with a hardware component that will soon be available: a $179 wearable band.

That makes Persona somewhat more like Bee, the wearable AI device that Amazon acquired in 2025 , but Persona’s device differs in several ways, Yadegari tells TechCrunch. For one, it won’t be ambient AI, meaning it won’t always be listening and recording. The band will have a button that activates the assistant, or it can be set up to activate with the flick of one’s wrist.

Yadegari also says that Persona is designed with user privacy in mind. Persona doesn’t run its AI model or store user data on the device. Instead, the model runs in Persona’s cloud, and user data is sent there. The assistant protects privacy by encrypting data in transit and at rest. Users can also delete their data, the company says.

In this way, it is promising that user conversations stay private and cannot be sold to advertisers or data brokers.

The team is also baking in safeguards to protect the assistant against phishing and prompt-injection attempts, Yadegari says. These are two areas that can plague agents, say AI labs like OpenAI.

Plus, he promises that Persona’s agent can’t see a user’s credit-card details and that purchases will require the user’s approval, with payment handled through external providers such as Stripe Link. Link is Stripe’s secure wallet designed for use by agents.

Although user data won’t be sold to advertisers, the startup’s current business model does rely on ads. Yadegari says the company will show advertised wares during shopping research. But he says that the agent will present unbiased recommendations because the agent won’t know which of the items are advertised. For example, if someone is researching office chairs, he says, “the agent knows their preferences” and will show them chairs that match those preferences, some of them sponsored results.

The bands are expected to be available in December, and an app is in the works. In the meantime, Persona has launched as a free beta product in which users work with the assistant via iMessage text messages. It has attracted “a few thousand beta users,” Yadegari said. The band has also already generated “five figures in preorder revenue.”

Like other consumer AI assistants, he says, Persona can order food or rides, take notes, book travel, answer questions and emails, among other tasks.

Eventually, he hopes to make Persona even more proactive. “It can offer help and solve problems before you even know you have a problem, and overall be more seamless with your life, so that you don’t need to stare at a rectangle in your hand all day.”

items.title: Can you trust Meta’s Muse or OpenAI’s Dots to run your life?
items.summary: My Decoder guest today is Hayden Field, The Verge’s senior AI reporter, and we’re discussing the new wave of consumer-friendly AI agents. If you’ve been paying attention to this space, you know AI enthusiasts have been using agents for a minute now — homebrew OpenClaw setups led
items.content:
The future of computing might be always-on, autonomous agents, but should we hand Meta or OpenAI this much persona data?

My Decoder guest today is Hayden Field, The Verge ’s senior AI reporter, and we’re discussing the new wave of consumer-friendly AI agents.

If you’ve been paying attention to this space, you know AI enthusiasts have been using agents for a minute now — homebrew OpenClaw setups led to a surge in Mac Mini sales earlier this year. But the launch of Meta’s Muse, OpenAI’s Dots, and xAI’s Grok bot has brought easy to use agents to millions.

Muse and Dots have had the highest-profile product launches, and they’re fascinating to pit against each other. Both Meta and OpenAI have decided to pitch these agents to mainstream users and businesses in the form of cute, animated mascots .

These can do everything from the boring — restaurant reservations and inbox triage — to more sophisticated tasks. In OpenAI’s cases, the company is even offering “specialist” Dots for marketing, legal work, and accounting.

Muse, notably, is free, while Dots are not. So you’ll hear Hayden and me get into why Meta, which still doesn’t have a frontier model of its own, might have a meaningful edge here because it’s so much better at making and distributing consumer products.

There’s also a huge Decoder -style tension wrapped up in the agent race: a conversation about what AI is good at today, what it still can’t do, and then the privacy and security implications of handing over your credit card information, your email inbox, and other sensitive hard drive data to an AI that might be able to do things for you without every requiring an app or a phone in your hand.

That might be the future of all computing, but it’s not at all clear if most people want to hand over the data to make it happen.

Okay: The Verge ’s Hayden Field on Muse, Dots, and trusting AI agents. Here we go.

This interview has been lightly edited for length and clarity.

Hayden Field, you’re the senior AI reporter here at The Verge . Welcome back to Decoder .

I’m excited to talk to you. This time there isn’t any wild interpersonal drama. No one’s feelings have been hurt. I would say Elon Musk tried to hurt some feelings and didn’t get there. Alexandr Wang from Meta has maybe been taking some shots, but none of the Real Housewives stuff we usually end up talking about when you’re on the show.

It’s been a bit of a pause in the soap opera antics for now, which I’m really grateful for.

Yeah, just some good old-fashioned product competition in the marketplace. Let’s see who wins and loses, and maybe everything will kill us all in the end. But, for now, cute mascots.

There’s a lot going on. Let’s start at the start. Hayden, you were at OpenAI DevDay in San Francisco. The company announced Dots, which is their new agent platform with a cute mascot. That happened just a few weeks after Meta Connect, at which the company was all in on Muse, their agent platform with an adorable mascot.

Tell us about the state of the industry right now. Everyone’s very excited about agents. What’s going on?

It’s funny to me because I’ve been covering agents for so long. I remember that in 2022, it was the year of ideation — that’s what tech leaders called it, referring to agents. They were just ideating. They were thinking about what it could look like. There were a lot of references to Jarvis from the Marvel Universe.

They called 2023 the year of deployment: “Let’s try things, let’s deploy and learn more about what’s failing.” Which meant pretty much all of them were failing at the time. Then we had 2024 and 2025. They didn’t have any names for those years, but agents were still pretty bad, as we saw.

2026 seems, to me, like the year of the beginnings of actually useful AI agents for the consumer, like always-on autonomous agents. Obviously, OpenAI was the start of all of this. But what’s interesting to me is that one man, Peter Steinberger, was able to create an actually useful AI agent for the consumer with OpenClaw — an always-on tool, despite its privacy flaws. It had a lot of privacy and security issues.

But it was an agent that was useful enough that people still wanted to use it anyway and try to find ways around these privacy issues that it was having. That inspired these companies to say, “If one man can do this over the course of one weekend, we’ve really been slacking. We have to get it together.”

OpenAI hired that guy, and now we have Dots. Meta, of course, was working on its own version of this and put it out sooner with Muse. They’re basically both always-on, autonomous AI agents that these companies are peddling as a way to be your personal assistant in a lot of ways.

The idea is to use them for booking flights, booking dinner reservations, buying gifts for people, but not only that. Some of them, Dots in particular, are kind of going further to be your work personal assistant and we’ll get into that in a minute.

But this is where OpenAI and Meta are warring right now. They’re trying to present these two AI agents as a little bit different from each other, even though they’re essentially the same.

Just broadly speaking, to define some terms, we’re gonna keep saying “agent,” and what we mean here is an AI model wrapped in a harness that lets it use a computer.

Right. The way that I describe AI agents usually is an AI tool that can complete multi-step complex tasks on your behalf without you hand-holding it the whole time.

I was a personal assistant in one of my first jobs in New York, so I would’ve gotten fired if every time my boss asked me to book a flight for her, I said, “What time? Also, what’s your SkyMiles number? Also, what’s your loyalty number again, for this other thing? Oh, do you want me to try to get you first class?”

items.title: Amazon’s new Kids Tablets let parents manage access to the Google Play store
items.summary: Alongside its new collection of Alexa Tablets that run Android with full access to the Google Play store, Amazon is introducing kid versions with similar functionality but the ability for parents to limit what software and content they have access to. The Amazon Kids Tablets also
items.content:
Amazon is introducing kid-friendly versions of its new Alexa Tablets with parental controls and curated content.

Alongside its new collection of Alexa Tablets that run Android with full access to the Google Play store, Amazon is introducing kid versions with similar functionality but the ability for parents to limit what software and content they have access to. The Amazon Kids Tablets also come with two different styles of colorful cases featuring characters from Paw Patrol, Barbie, and SpongeBob: a thicker more protective option for pre-kindergarten children, and a thinner one for kids aged six and up.

The Amazon Kids Tablets are available in two sizes that both feature lightweight aluminum designs and 8-core processors and seem identical to the smaller versions of the new Alexa Tablets, but with added software. The Kids Tablet 8.7-inch starts at $229.99 and comes with 64GB of storage and a battery good for up to 14 hours of video playback. The larger Amazon Kids Tablet 11-inch starts at $329.99 and features a better 2.5K display, 8GB of RAM for improved gaming experiences, and stylus support. Both will be available for preorder soon with shipping starting on October 14th in the US.

All versions of the Kids Tablet comes with a one-year subscription to Amazon Kids Plus which includes a collection of ad-free content including books, TV shows, games, apps, and audiobooks from companies like Disney, Nickelodeon, and Lego. Amazon is also introducing a new feature to Kids Plus called Storybuilder that uses AI to generate picture books and comics from descriptions of characters, worlds, and plot twists provided by kids.

Amazon’s Parent Dashboard comes pre-installed on the new Kids Tablets allowing them to set screen-time limits, monitor usage, and set learning goals that prioritize educational apps and games over entertainment. All of the settings in Parent Dashboard can also be accessed remotely through iOS and Android apps, including approval for every download from the Google Play Store.

에이전트(agent)를 비롯해 인공지능(AI) 시대 핵심 키워드로 된 최상위 도메인 선점 경쟁이 치열하게 벌어지고 있다.

올해 국제인터넷주소관리기구(ICANN)에 접수된 일반 최상위 도메인(gTLD) 신청 건수가 총 1615건으로 집계됐다고 더레지스터가 7일(현지시간) 보도했다.

보도에 따르면 ICANN이 4월 30일부터 8월 12일까지 신규 gTLD를 신청 접수를 받았다. 그 결과 481개 신청자가 1615건을 신청했다.

gTLD는 닷컴, 닷넷 같은 최상위 도메인을 의미한다. ICANN이 신규 gTLD 접수를 받은 것은 2012년 이후 처음이다. ICANN은 2012년에는 총 1200건의 신규 gTLD를 승인했다.

이번 gTLD 신청에서 특히 관심을 끄는 것은 AI관련 도메인이다.

오픈AI가 닷챗지피티(.chatgpt), 닷agi를 비롯한 15개 최상위 도메인을 신청했다. 닷agi는 일반인공지능(artificial general intelligence)을 상징하는 도메인이다. 또 모델 컨텍스트 프로토콜(MCP)을 상징하는 닷mcp도 신청했다. 이 도메인은 구글을 비롯해 다른 4개 회사도 경쟁을 하고 있다.

가장 치열한 경쟁이 벌어지고 있는 것은 닷에이전트이다. 현재 닷에이전트 도메인은 메타, 구글을 비롯해 13개 업체가 경쟁을 벌이고 있다.

초지능을 의미하는 슈퍼인텔리전스 도메인도 인기다. 현재 닷슈퍼인텔리전스는 메타를 비롯한 6개 업체들이 신청해 치열한 선점경쟁을 벌이고 있다.

AI 기업들이 고유 브랜드 도메인 확보 움직임도 활발하다. 앤트로픽은 회사명은 닷앤트로픽과 닷클로드(.claude)를 신청했다. 마이크로소프트는 닷코파일럿과 기업명인 닷msft를 신청했다. 블루스카이도 닷bsky 확보에 나섰다.

지역별로는 북미 쪽이 864를 신청해 가장 많았으며, 유럽인들이 506개로 그 뒤를 이었다. 아시아 태평양은 218개, 아프리카는 16개로 집계됐다. 반면 라틴아메리타와 카리브해 지역 신청 건수는 11개에 불과했다.

이번에 신청된 도메인은 ‘문자열 확정의 날(String Confirmation Day)’인 11월 7일까지 결정될 예정이다. 도메인 주인이 결정된 뒤에는 최상위 도메인 관리 기관을 설립한 뒤 등록 작업을 시작하게 된다.

절차대로 진행될 경우 이번에 승인되는 신규 최상위 도메인은 내년부터 등록 가능하게 될 전망이다.

items.title: Google releases a new local-first Granola competitor
items.summary: Google’s new AI Edge Foresight app takes on Granola with an offline meeting note-taker that can transcribe conversations, generate notes, and answer questions using on-device AI.
items.content:
Earlier in April, Google released an AI-powered dictation tool that worked with local models . Now, the same team has released a new competitor to the AI note-taker Granola and others, which it calls Google AI Edge Foresight .

The Mac app can work completely offline, utilizing the on-device EmbeddingGemma 2 model, with 740 million parameters, to capture meeting notes across apps, including those from in-person meetings.

The app is similar to the popular AI note-taker Granola because it has a split-screen view with the ability to write shorthand notes on one side and AI-generated notes on the other side.

Like Granola, it also lets you take manual notes while transcribing the meeting. Plus, in Google’s app, you can view the transcript of the meeting or chat with the Gemma 4-powered assistant to get answers.

In addition, users can upload documents including PDFs, Google Docs, Microsoft Office formats, plain text, Markdown, and web bookmarks to build a knowledge base. Using your meeting notes and documents, the app can answer questions in real time if a point related to data in the knowledge base comes up.

On its FAQ page, the company specified that Google AI Edge Foresight is optimized for Apple Silicon and can completely work offline. This means you can work with your meeting notes when you are traveling or in a place without an internet connection.

While Google’s earlier dictation app was an experimental one that didn’t make it to mainstream usage, its new meeting note-taker could be just to showcase the ability of its Gemma series of offline models.

However, Google could very well release a consumer version of meeting note-taker that works across video calling apps through its Gemini apps while relying on its cloud models.

The meeting note-taker space is competitive and crowded. But that hasn’t stopped companies from creating their own tools. In the last few months, dictation company Wispr and scheduling company Calendly released their own note-takers. Meanwhile, productivity startup Superhuman (formerly Grammarly) acquired YC-backed note-taker Fathom last month.

items.title: China’s Manus raises over $500M in first funding round since split with Meta
items.summary: Boyu Capital and IDG Capital led the funding round, and existing shareholders Tencent, HSG (formerly known as Sequoia China), ZhenFund, and others also participated.
items.content:
Chinese AI lab Manus’ parent company, Butterfly Effect, said on Thursday in a WeChat post that it has raised more than $500 million, the company’s first funding round since Meta was forced to call off its $2 billion acquisition of the startup.

Boyu Capital and IDG Capital led the funding round, and existing shareholders Tencent, HSG (formerly known as Sequoia China), ZhenFund, and others also participated. The AI company said it will continue hiring both at home and abroad.

Manus did not disclose its valuation, but last month was said to be in talks with investors to raise $500 million at a $4 billion valuation.

Manus, which went viral following a demo of its AI agent last year, relocated its staff to Singapore in mid-2025 before announcing a $2 billion acquisition deal with Meta that December. The startup was said to be pulling in annual recurring revenue of over $100 million at the time.

In April, Chinese authorities ordered the AI startup to unwind the deal amid intensifying worries in China over losing AI talent and researchers to the West.

Manus in August resumed independent operations following the end of the Meta deal, and said it was required to delete some user data as part of the split. The company is also reported to be considering going public in Hong Kong, according to the report.

Manus did not respond to TechCrunch’s questions about its valuation.

Manus makes AI products and agents similar to what companies like Cursor, Lovable, and Replit offer. It offers a chatbot and vibe-coding tools to let users build apps and websites, create designs and presentations, generate video, and more.

The company recently launched Manus 2.0 , which it says brings a new architecture with new products and capabilities built around a new harness. It also introduced Cue, a stand-alone app that gives personal AI agents their own email addresses, phone numbers, digital wallets, and computers. The app lets agents communicate, handle tasks across services, and make payments within limits set by the user.

items.title: Amazon unveils new Alexa tablets with Alexa+ and Google Play Store access
items.summary: The lineup includes three models: Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, Amazon Alexa Tablet 11, and Amazon Alexa Tablet 8.
items.content:
Amazon on Thursday unveiled a new lineup of Alexa tablets that feature personalized intelligence from its Alexa+ AI assistant and full access to the Google Play Store. The lineup includes three models: Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, Amazon Alexa Tablet 11, and Amazon Alexa Tablet 8.

The tech giant says each tablet features an aluminum unibody design, high-resolution displays, and runs on Android. Plus, with access to the Google Play Store at launch, users will be able to download millions of apps, including YouTube, Netflix, Gmail, and more.

Until now, Amazon’s tablets have run Fire OS and ship with its own app store. With these new tablets, however, Amazon is taking a different approach to reach a wider audience. An Amazon spokesperson told TechCrunch that these are an all-new product line with new hardware and a new OS, rather than a rebrand of Fire Tablets.

The Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro measures 6.5 mm thick and is engineered for “perfect balance,” Amazon explained in a press release. It houses a 12-inch, 280 PPI display, a 120Hz refresh rate, and a 3:2 aspect ratio for more usable screen space, which the company says is perfect for reading, watching, or working. It comes in two display options: a standard display and a Nanomatte display with anti-glare.

Amazon says the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro delivers nearly three times the processing performance and nine times the graphics performance of any tablet it has shipped before. The company says the tablet can easily handle everything from multi-window multitasking and graphics-intensive gaming to 4K streaming. It features Dolby Atmos speakers, Wi-Fi 6E, and 16 hours of video playback.

The company also announced the Alexa Tablet Pro Pen and Pro Keyboard, which Amazon says are designed to turn the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro into a full workstation.

The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro starts at $499.99, while the Nanomatte model starts at $549.99. The tablet comes in Graphite.

The new tablets are launching with built-in access to Alexa+. Users will be able to say “Alexa” or tap the “Ask Alexa” button to get answers to questions, control their smart home, and more. With On-Screen Intelligence, users will be able to ask Alexa to look at what’s on screen to receive contextual help. For example, while browsing a list of trails, users can ask Alexa, “Which of these hikes is best for me?”

The Alexa Tablet 11 is an 11-inch device with a 2.5K display at 276 pixels per inch, 90Hz smooth scrolling, and a 16:10 aspect ratio. The tech giant says it’s designed for streaming, gaming, reading, and browsing. It features 15 hours of video playback and dual Dolby Atmos speakers. It starts at $329.99 and comes in Graphite, Amethyst, and Matcha.

The Alexa Tablet 8 is the smallest and most portable of the three, featuring an 8.7-inch display and an all-aluminum design that weighs 329 grams. It’s designed to be held in one hand and carried anywhere for reading, browsing, and streaming on the go, Amazon says. It starts at $229.99 and comes in Graphite, Rosette, and Teal.

All of the new tablets are launching with a new Kindle reading experience. When users open the Kindle app, notifications are silenced, blue light is reduced, and battery life can last up to 20 hours.

The company also announced on Wednesday that it’s launching new Amazon Kids Tablets , with 8.7-inch and 11-inch sizes available. Bundles include a tablet, a kid-proof case, and a year of Amazon Kids+, which provides access to thousands of kid-friendly books, games, videos, and apps in an ad-free environment.

There are separate versions for pre-K kids (ages 3+) and kids 6+, as younger kids get a soft bumper case in designs from franchises like Paw Patrol and Barbie, while older kids get a slim hard case with a built-in kickstand.

All three Amazon Alexa Tablets and the Amazon Kids Tablets will go on sale October 14, 2026, in the U.S., Mexico, and Canada. They’ll launch in the U.K., Germany, France, Italy, and Spain on October 19, while the Amazon Kids Tablets will also be available in Japan starting October 14.

items.title: Hands-on with Amazon’s Alexa Tablet 12 Pro and its wild new matte display
items.summary: Amazon's Fire tablets are notable for being dirt cheap. While they're great for kids, they don't offer a premium Android tablet experience. The company's new $499 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro is an attempt to build a device someone might actually want to use. It's one of a few new Android
items.content:
The Alexa line is also Amazon’s first tablet to run full-fledged Android with access to the Play Store.

If you buy something from a link, The Verge may earn a commission. See our ethics statement.

Amazon’s Fire tablets are notable for being dirt cheap. While they’re great for kids , they don’t offer a premium Android tablet experience. The company’s new $499 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro is an attempt to build a device someone might actually want to use. It’s one of a few new Android tablets Amazon announced today, and it’s the one you need to know about.

The screen is the truly exciting thing about the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro. The $549.99 Alexa Tablet 12 Pro has a 12.3-inch 3:2 display that can be configured with Corning’s Nanomatte tech, similar to Apple’s nano-texture, which reduces glare and gives the screen a more paper-like feel.

It’s impossible to do it justice in photos or video. The Nanomatte coating doesn’t simply reduce glare; it almost completely eliminates it. Amazon held a briefing in a brightly sunlit room, and I thought the 12 Pro was a dummy unit when I first saw it. It looked like a cardboard placeholder image was placed inside. Then an Amazon rep started swiping around the screen.

There’s also a standard glossy option, and the difference is shocking. In the bright sunlight of the room, the glossy screen was basically a mirror and was easily washed out when viewed at an angle. The Nanomatte display, however, was clearly readable at any angle and barely reflected any ambient light. Only at extreme angles in the brightest patches of light did it become difficult to see.

The screen pairs particularly well with the immersive Kindle mode. Here, background activities are limited, notifications are silenced, and blue light is lowered to reduce eye strain. There are three different Kindle-specific display modes. Standard delivers the full vibrancy of the screen; Color offers a softer, more muted experience; and Ink is full grayscale. In Kindle mode, battery life is also extended from 16 hours to 20 hours.

Without having the two side-by-side, it’s hard to say how it compares to Apple’s matte display on the iPad Pro, but anecdotally it seems to retain slightly more contrast. Using a stylus with it is much more pleasant than on a glossy display, but I can’t say I noticed a difference between it and an iPad.

The Alexa Tablet Pro Pen and Pro Keyboard attach magnetically and seem serviceable enough. I wouldn’t want to type on its shallow, cramped keys all day, but they’re fine for knocking out a few emails. The keyboard case was a little clunky to get on and off, though. It’s actually two parts — the back cover and stand are separate from the keyboard base.

Amazon keeps some of Alexa’s more invasive features off by default. On-Screen Intelligence, which can see what you’re doing and take actions based on what’s actually on your screen, is strictly opt-in. There are also robust controls for limiting what Alexa can hear and remember.

If you do opt in, though, Alexa becomes a pretty powerful shopping companion. I was able to open random photos from the internet and ask Alexa to find me something in them, like a coffee table or a mirror, and, even if it couldn’t track down the exact thing, it found something close. Then it would add it to my Amazon cart if I asked. How likely am I to ask Alexa to track down a bathroom fixture for me from a Pinterest photo and deliver it to my house in two days via Prime? Not very. I’m also unlikely to have it automatically add school holidays to my calendar from the Department of Education site, but it will if you ask it to.

The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro starts at $499.99 , but you’ll have to shell out at least $549.99 for the Nanomatte model. If you want to tack on the keyboard case and the Pro Pen, that will be an additional $149.99 and $89.99 , respectively.

Amazon also announced two smaller models that lack the Nanomatte screen options. The Alexa Tablet 11 starts at $329.99 , while the Alexa Tablet 8 starts at $229.99 . Those come in more fun colorways, including rosette and matcha, in addition to the drab but functional graphite of the Tablet 12 Pro.

items.title: Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, Alexa Tablet 11, Alexa Tablet 8: Specs, Features, Price
items.summary: The three new aluminum Alexa Tablets now run Android with full access to the Google Play Store. There are versions for kids too.
items.content:
The era of Amazon's Fire tablets —cheap slate computers ranging from $60 to $280—is over.

All of the Fire tablets are being replaced by the all-aluminum Amazon Alexa Tablet. These tablets will, in a first for Amazon, run official Android and have full access to the Google Play Store. The lack of proper app support was always a sticking point for the Fire tablets, which ran a custom version of Android and had a much more limited app library .

The new Alexa Tablet series comes in three models: the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro ($500) , Alexa Tablet 11 ($330) , and Alexa Tablet 8 ($230) , with the numbers corresponding to the display size. Amazon is also offering kids' editions of the latter two devices at the same prices. These include bumper cases for extra protection, a one-year, worry-free guarantee to replace the device if it breaks, and a year of Amazon Kids+ service to fill the tablet with age-appropriate content .

As for Fire tablets, Amazon says it will stop shipping the devices in the next month or two. It will support them for four years from the last ship date. Amazon is committing to at least four years of software updates for the new Alexa tablets, which will launch with Android 16 and will receive Android 17 early in 2027. Preorders for the new Alexa Tablets are open now, and they'll begin shipping on October 14.

From left to right: The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, the Alexa Tablet 11, and the Alexa Tablet 8.

The experience is largely the same on all three tablets, with aluminum builds designed to mimic the new aluminum Kindles . The MediaTek Dimensity 8189 chip powers the two smaller tablets, whereas the 12-inch device gets a little more power from the MediaTek Dimensity 8400.

The Alexa Tablet 12 Pro is the outlier of the trio, as it's the only one with two display variants: a standard 12-inch LCD screen or a 12-inch Nanomatte display with anti-glare and anti-reflective properties. Upgrade to the Nanomatte—starting at $550—for a matte, paperlike look and feel. With a peak brightness of 500 nits, it should still be bright enough to view in sunlight.

Amazon says it developed this screen in partnership with Corning (the company that makes most of the glass that protects smartphone displays). It's similar to the matte displays found on devices like TCL's Nxtpaper series , though Amazon's vice president of devices, Kevin Keith, says the hexagon-shaped imprint on the Nanomatte display can push out vivid colors and crisp blacks while still retaining those matte properties.

The screen also offers a “really good” writing experience, according to Keith. He says the same engineers who worked on the Kindle Scribe worked with Corning to get that paperlike feel. The screen works with Amazon's new Alexa Tablet Pro Pen ($90), which has 4,096 levels of pressure sensitivity, plus tilt detection. The pen can magnetically dock to the top of the slate for charging and pairing. Amazon also sells a Pro Keyboard ($150) for the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro, which attaches to the device via the pogo pins on the bottom edge—no Bluetooth needed.

Now that Android has recently gained multiwindowing features , attaching the keyboard turns the largest Alexa tablet into a productivity machine: split apps across the screen, resize them into various windows, and “save” several desktop arrangements so you can pick up where you left off.

For the kids’ versions of the Alexa Tablet 11 and Alexa Tablet 8 , Amazon says the software is still Android with a heavily customized interface for kid-friendly content and built-in parental controls. Keith says one in five kids in the US has an Amazon tablet, so it'll be interesting to see how that changes now that these devices start at a higher price .

It may look and feel like Android, but Amazon has tweaked the interface to make these Alexa Tablets feel like Amazon hardware.

The Amazon Alexa Tablet 12 Pro is on the top left, with its Nanomatte display. The Alexa Tablet 11 sits below in Kindle mode, and the Alexa Tablet 8 is on the right.

The top-left corner of the home screen features a persistent widget called the Dynamic Tab. This scrollable widget lets you dive into Amazon content you may have been consuming on another device—say, if you were reading on your Kindle, watching a movie on Prime Video on your iPhone, or snapped some photos and you want to view them on Amazon Photos.

Swipe right, and instead of Google's Discover feed, you're instead greeted with Amazon's For You experience. Amazon's Fire tablets were a vehicle to put Amazon content in front of your eyeballs, and that hasn't changed with the Alexa Tablets. Again, you can continue consuming content here, with tabs for movies and TV, games, and Kindle. There's also a news feed, and you can tap Alexa prompts for more information on a story.

Uniquely, opening the Kindle app triggers “Kindle mode,” which disables all notifications, turns on the blue light filter, and extends battery life to 20 hours (less on the smaller tablets). You can also choose one of three display treatments in this mode: subtle warmth with natural color, a softened paper tone, or monochrome. There's even a fun page-turn effect that mimics turning a page in a book. As soon as you exit the app, notifications turn back on, and the screen returns to normal. Annotations you make with the stylus will sync with Kindle apps on pen-supported devices, like the Kindle Scribe.

In the bottom-right corner, a persistent “Ask Alexa” chat box lets you call up the virtual assistant immediately. You can also trigger it by saying, “Alexa,” just like an Echo device . It can control your smart home devices, but the marquee addition is Alexa's On-Screen Intelligence. It's opt-in—with an on-screen indicator whenever it's active—allowing the assistant to see what you're looking at and answer contextual questions.

items.title: Uber and China’s Pony.ai plan to launch robotaxis in London
items.summary: The two companies said on Thursday that they would begin testing Pony.ai's Gen-7 robotaxis in London in the coming weeks.
items.content:
Uber and Chinese autonomous vehicle maker Pony.ai plan to launch a robotaxi service in London as part of an expanded partnership to bring driverless cars to Europe. The two companies said on Thursday that they would begin testing Pony.ai’s Gen-7 robotaxis in London in the coming weeks.

The announcement is the latest instance of Uber’s ambitious push into autonomous vehicle technology through a growing web of partnerships and investments. The ride-hailing company has struck deals with more than 30 autonomous vehicle companies , including Pony.ai, over the past few years as it seeks to capture a share of the autonomous delivery and ride-hailing markets.

Uber expects to offer AV trips in as many as 15 cities globally by the end of 2026, roughly split between U.S. and international markets.

Uber and Pony.ai first partnered in May 2025, initially focusing on the Middle East . The relationship has since expanded to Europe, where it plans to deploy 2,000 robotaxis, starting with Croatia’s capital, Zagreb .

In August 2026, the companies launched an autonomous ride-hailing service in Zagreb with a third partner, Verne. Under that arrangement, Pony.ai supplies the autonomous driving system and the Arcfox Alpha T5 robotaxi, developed with Chinese automaker BAIC. Verne, a startup set up by Rimac Group founder and CEO Mate Rimac, owns and operates the fleet, while Uber provides access to its vast ride-hailing network.

The London service will follow a similar model, although the companies have not said who will own and operate the fleet.

Pony.ai won’t be Uber’s only robotaxi partner in London. The company has also partnered with and invested in British self-driving startup Wayve, and plans to launch a robotaxi service in the city.

In February 2026, Wayve raised $1.2 billion in a funding round that saw investments from Microsoft, Nvidia, and Uber. The total funding in that round could reach $1.5 billion thanks to an additional $300 million from Uber , contingent on Wayve deploying robotaxis, starting in London.

Uber has pursued this multi-partner strategy elsewhere. In Dubai, for instance, it has struck separate deals with Baidu and WeRide to launch robotaxi services.

Pony.ai, meanwhile, has launched robotaxi services in four Chinese cities and secured partnerships with local transportation authorities as it works to expand into European and Middle Eastern markets, including Qatar.

items.summary: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. AI breakthroughs in robotics won’t change your life any time soon The hype around humanoid robots is reaching fever pitch. Much of it comes fr
items.content:
The hype around humanoid robots is reaching fever pitch. Much of it comes from the idea that the same AI advances behind ChatGPT and Claude could enable robots to imitate human movement the way chatbots imitate human language. But many researchers are skeptical.

They argue that such assumptions minimize the challenges of using an intelligence built on language and images to master the infinite variability of the physical world. They also point out that conflating humanoids with so-called generalist machines is misleading.

Across robotics labs, tensions have emerged over whether current forms of AI are all that’s needed to perfect all-purpose humanoids or whether an entirely new path is required.

Read the full story on what it will take to build truly general-purpose robots .

As sea levels rise and flood risks worsen, WaveSave has emerged with an ingeniously simple tool: a portable rubber dam that’s quick to install when flooding starts.

Anyone can unfurl the SlamDam on the ground along a riverbank or shoreline and pump it full of water until it swells into place. And there it stands, up to 1.3 meters high, shielding nearby property or structures from damage as waters rise.

WaveSave now plans to take its unusual approach to flood protection much further .

Our Climate Tech Companies to Watch list is always a little ray of hope for me—there are some fascinating ideas out there about how we power our world or move away from fossil fuels.

Our chosen companies also reflect several aspects of the current moment. One is that China is the center of the climate and energy tech world. Another is that everybody wants a piece of the data center pie. And then there’s the fact that the grid needs support, with energy storage a key piece moving forward.

Here’s what this year’s list reveals about the state of climate tech .

독학 개발자 시길 웬(Sigil Wen)이 설립한 스타트업 콘웨이 리서치가 기기 안에서만 실행되는 AI 비서 '언더독(Underdog)'의 초대제 베타를 공개했다. 현지 시각 10월 6일 테크크런치에 따르면 언더독은 사용자의 데이터를 외부 서버로 전송하지 않고 사용자가 이미 보유한 기기에서 처리하는 온디바이스 방식이다. 현재 맥과 윈도우 PC를 지원하며 리눅스·아이폰·안드로이드 버전은 준비하고 있다.

웬은 AI 모델을 실행하는 추론 엔진 '허스키(Husky)'를 직접 개발했다. 그는 다른 온디바이스 엔진과 달리 컴퓨터의 중앙처리장치와 그래픽 칩 사이에서 이동하는 데이터 양을 줄여 속도를 높였다고 설명했다. 사용자가 접근을 허용한 이메일 등 계정의 인증 키도 암호화해 보관한다.

언더독은 큐원3.8 27B를 미세조정한 매개변수 270억 개 규모 추론 모델을 사용한다. 미세조정은 이미 학습한 모델을 특정 목적에 맞춰 추가로 학습시키는 과정이다. 데이터센터에서 실행되는 최신 대형 모델보다 작지만, 웬은 이 모델이 일부 벤치마크에서 6개월 전 최고 성능 모델이던 클로드 오퍼스 4.6과 비슷한 결과를 냈다고 밝혔다. 그는 쇼핑 정보 조사나 수학 숙제 풀이 같은 일상 작업을 처리하기에 충분한 성능이라고 주장했다.

투자자로는 스트라이프 공동창업자 패트릭 콜리슨과 안드레센 호로위츠(a16z), 코슬라 벤처스, SV 엔젤, 멘로 벤처스와 앤트로픽이 함께 운영하는 앤솔로지 펀드가 참여했다. 버셀 창업자 기예르모 라우치와 오픈AI 연구원 노암 브라운도 엔젤 투자자로 참여했다. 웬은 17세에 실리콘밸리로 이주해 안드레이 카르파시와 같은 AI 해커하우스에서 생활했고, 현재 피터 틸이 운영하는 틸 펠로십 회원이다.

Vesta raises $30M to bring swarms of agents to mortgage lenders
items.summary: Vesta, an AI-native software startup that helps lenders originate mortgages, announced a $30 million round led by Conversion Capital.
items.content:
Vesta , an AI-native software startup that helps lenders originate mortgages, announced on Thursday that it raised a $30 million round led by Conversion Capital.

The startup uses AI agents to automate much of the loan origination process, which, the founders say, helps lenders reduce the time and costs of processing mortgages. Three of the company’s customers, including Pennymac and New American Funding, also invested in the round alongside Citi Ventures and Andreessen Horowitz.

Mike Yu co-founded the company in 2020 with Devon Yang. Yu, the company’s CEO, told TechCrunch that now was the perfect time to raise because demand for the product has “exploded in the last year.” He said revenue is up 12x year over year. The company has raised $85 million in funding to date.

“While the traction is great, we are still under 5% market share and now is the time to staff up, take the market, and invest in new product lines,” Yu said.

Those new product lines include a personal assistant for mortgage issuers that can help perform tasks and track workflows. It takes around 40 days to close a mortgage in the U.S., costing around $11,000 per loan. “Most of that cost is human labor, and a major bottleneck in the timeline is just waiting for a person to get to reviewing your loan.”

With Vesta, the idea is to allow humans to deploy a swarm of agents to speed completion of tasks. Customers decide what tasks they want to assign the Vesta agents: “Many of our customers start an AI agent with a person approving its work, then let it handle a share of loans on its own, then expand,” Yu explained, adding that some lenders are even using Vesta AI agents to make mortgage underwriting decisions.

Companies remain responsible for underwriting decisions, he said, regardless of what software or AI agents they use, and Yu added that all actions and reasoning behind a decision are recorded for compliance and to audit AI decisions.

This level of autonomy stems from the vast improvements in AI models in the past year, which weren’t good enough, at that time, to build agents for the complex multi-stage tasks involved in mortgage lending. Before, the company was just focused on building the right data architecture to use the most advanced tools to automate the mortgage process.

“For us, the big breakthrough was [Claude] Sonnet 4.5, which we just found to be much better at adhering to user-configured instructions over the time horizons we need than previous generations,” Yu said.

Vesta is, in many ways, competing against both traditional mortgage systems like ICE Mortgage Technology and other AI-native companies also trying to automate the mortgage lending process, like Xpanse .

At least against legacy incumbents, Yu said Vesta’s advantage is that those companies weren’t built for AI agents, and “putting AI agents on top of them is very hard,” he said. As for what’s next, “our priority is earning the business of the rest of the mortgage industry,” Yu said. “Then, we’ll go wherever our customers take us.”

items.title: Nvidia's big bet on physical AI aims for safer robotaxis, humanoid robots
items.summary: Full-stack safety solution for physical AI is being used by robotics companies.
items.content:
Investors bullish on AI data centers may be fueling Nvidia’s multitrillion-dollar market capitalization, but the AI chipmaker has also bet billions of dollars on physical AI technologies such as robotics and self-driving cars. Part of that gambit has involved developing a full-stack safety system that companies can build upon to reduce the risk of their machines harming nearby people.

Nvidia’s Halos system launched in 2025 with hardware and software tools to help developers implement guardrails in self-driving cars and other autonomous vehicles. Then the company expanded its safety architecture to more physical AI technologies by announcing Nvidia Halos for Robotics in June 2026—with the goal of enabling safe deployments of autonomous mobile robots in warehouses, humanoid robots walking around inside a factory, or even surgical robots.

“Now the AI models are getting capable, the robot hardware is getting capable, and a thing we thought is going to be the next bottleneck is safety,” Amit Goel , head of robotics ecosystem and edge computing at Nvidia, told Ars. “So that’s why we launched our Halos for Robotics to unlock the capability of these systems.”

The expanded safety offering for robotics comes as Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang described the physical AI business as already driving nearly $10 billion in annual revenue for the company during an appearance on the All-In Podcast in March 2026. Huang began highlighting physical AI as Nvidia’s second-most important growth category in 2025.

The tech giant has also invested directly in multiple robotics companies, including the humanoid robotics startups Agility Robotics and Figure AI, along with companies developing robotics foundation models. NVIDIA has even partnered with the Chinese humanoid robotics company Unitree to provide an “open humanoid robot reference design” for researchers.

So what does Nvidia’s full-stack safety system for robotics involve? It starts with hardware, such as the Nvidia IGX Thor computing module for robotics and industrial applications that has an independent processor dedicated to safety-related workloads. “In the context of physical AI, you need to have your functional system and your safety system all running on the same silicon,” Goel said.

On the software side, the Halos operating system was designed to enable constant monitoring of “every hardware block” and “every software library” to swiftly spot any failures, Goel explained. The system also isolates safety-critical computing workloads to avoid any potential interference.

The system also includes the Nvidia Holoscan Sensor Bridge that connects sensor data with safety-related computer processing in a way that can easily identify corrupted data. This can be embedded in individual hardware components, like a microcontroller or Field Programmable Gate Array.

Last but not least, the Halos package also includes Nvidia’s simulations for testing robots in virtual environments, and an inspection lab program that allows robotics companies and other partners to get quick feedback on any safety “artifacts” that arise during robotic development.

However, adapting Nvidia Halos from autonomous vehicles to robotics required accommodating many different definitions of safety. The definition of functional safety for autonomous driving generally remains the same across different automotive companies and countries, Goel explained. But a robotic vacuum cleaning a hallway will have very different safety considerations compared to a robotic forklift handling heavy payloads in a warehouse loading dock.

“We had to reimagine and do a lot of foundational work to build a platform that is programmable, that gives all the hooks to the developers to actually define custom safety functions, but at the same time not break the underlying infrastructure that we built,” Goel told Ars. “Because giving flexibility can come at the cost of losing some control over the stack.”

Custom safety functions are also necessary because robots may operate in complex, diverse environments.

“If you are a robot coming down an aisle at six miles per hour, your senses do not see what are the blind spots and what is coming around the corner,” Gold said. “What the robots do is almost come to a halt before the turn, because they really don’t know what’s happening in all these factories, warehouses and hospitals—they’re unstructured environments and things can come from anywhere.”

The US startup Agility Robotics was first to incorporate Nvidia Halos into its latest Digit 5 humanoid robot, which is designed to work safely near people without requiring isolated workstations or physical barriers. The Nvidia system helped Agility bring all the relevant safety sensors and hardware inside the robot, whereas previous Digit robot operations have also relied on external sensors placed around the robot’s work cell to ensure safety.

“Now the robot is literally unchained—the safety goes with the robot wherever it goes,” Goel told Ars. “Now they can operate everywhere in a factory or a warehouse without having to set up a brand new infrastructure every time they want to do a new task.”

The Massachusetts-based robotics company Boston Dynamics has also been an early partner in the Nvidia Halos safety accreditation program , with a focus on building a safety platform that encompasses their Spot robot dogs, wheeled Stretch robots with a large robotic arm, and Atlas humanoid robots that could start deploying in the automotive factories of parent company Hyundai by 2028.

Other companies working to incorporate Nvidia Halos include the German company KION Group that deploys self-driving forklifts and other autonomous mobile robots, along with the South Korean company LG that is developing its own humanoid robot based on Nvidia’s IAI foundation model for humanoid robots called Isaac GROOT.

아부다비 아랍에미리트 , 2026년 10월 8일 /PRNewswire/ -- 세계에서 가장 규모가 크고 경험이 풍부한 액티브 투자 운용사 중 하나로 운용자산이 미화 3조 6000억 달러에 달하는 캐피탈 그룹(Capital Group)이 이날 아랍에미리트의 수도 아부다비의 국제 금융 센터인 ADGM의 금융서비스규제청(Financial Services Regulatory Authority, FSRA)으로부터 금융서비스 허가를 취득해 규제 대상 투자 운용사로 영업할 수 있게 됐다고 발표했다. 이번 승인으로 캐피탈 그룹은 ADGM 내에서 트레이딩, 투자 운용, 판매 활동을 수행할 수 있게 된다.

이번 규제상의 이정표는 2026년 5월 중동 첫 사무소를 아부다비에 설립할 계획을 발표한 데 이어, 이 지역에 대한 캐피탈 그룹의 장기적 의지가 다음 단계로 나아갔음을 보여준다. 캐피탈 그룹은 이후 북미, 유럽, 아시아의 직원들을 이전 배치해 투자, 운영, 고객 대응 전문성을 이 지역의 고객과 기회에 더 가까이 두었다. 현지 인력 규모는 사업과 고객의 필요에 따라 시간이 지나면서 늘어날 전망이다.

캐피탈 그룹의 벤노 클링엔베르크-팀(Benno Klingenberg-Timm) 아부다비 사무소 대표 겸 유럽 및 아시아 기관투자 부문 대표 는 다음과 같이 말했다. "아부다비에 규제 대상 거점을 마련함으로써 당사는 고객과, 우리가 오랜 기간 활동해 온 지역인 중동 전역의 투자 기회에 한층 더 가까워진다. 캐피탈 그룹은 첫날부터 현지에서 투자, 운영, 고객 대응 역량을 갖춘 의미 있는 거점을 운영할 것이다. 1989년 싱가포르 사무소를 열었을 때와 마찬가지로, 우리는 아부다비에 캐피탈 그룹의 폭넓은 전문성을 모두 결집하고 있으며, 이는 이 지역의 장기 성장에 대한 우리의 확신을 보여준다."

ADGM의 아흐메드 자심 알 자아비(Ahmed Jasim Al Zaabi) 회장 은 다음과 같이 말했다. "글로벌 투자 운용사인 캐피탈 그룹이 아부다비에 거점을 마련하게 된 것을 환영한다. 이번 결정은 아부다비 금융 생태계의 강점과, 이 지역 전반에서 장기적인 기회를 찾는 글로벌 기관들을 위한 선도적인 국제금융센터로서 ADGM이 넓혀 가는 입지를 보여준다."

캐피탈 그룹의 마이크 기틀린(Mike Gitlin) 사장 겸 최고경영자 는 다음과 같이 말했다. "중동은 캐피탈 그룹과 우리 고객에게 전략적으로 중요한 지역이다. 아부다비에서 규제 라이선스를 확보한 것은 이 지역에 대한 우리의 장기적 의지와, 선도적인 국제금융센터로서 지속될 발전에 대한 우리의 확신을 보여준다. 앞으로 고객 및 파트너와의 관계를 더욱 깊이 다져 나가길 기대한다."

Life Is Asymmetric. The Scientists Who Figured Out Why Won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry
items.summary: Henri Kagan and Kensō Soai designed chemical reactions producing only one of the two mirror-image forms of a molecule—an important finding for the synthesis of pharmaceuticals and other biological substances.
items.content:
The 2026 Nobel Prize in Chemistry was awarded to Henri Kagan and Kensō Soai for discovering a solution to the enigma of nature’s chemical asymmetry, a finding that opened up new avenues for manipulating the reactions used in manufacturing pharmaceuticals and other materials.

Some molecules are chiral, meaning a molecule has two forms that are mirror images of each other but not identical, like your left and right hand. One of the most mysterious chemical phenomena in biology is that living organisms contain almost exclusively one of the two forms. This is known as homochirality.

Both versions of the molecules—each called an enantiomer—have similar physical properties but can behave differently. The Nobel Committee used a simple analogy to explain this: A locksmith can create two mirror-image keys, but “only one of them fits the lock—and the lock can be damaged if your customers try to unlock it with the other key.”

In the development of new drugs that use, for example, amino acids or sugar molecules as a basis, homochirality poses a problem: While one of the enantiomers of these chiral molecules produces the desired therapeutic effect, the other can cause unnecessary and, at times, harmful side effects. Scientists can’t always easily control which version of the molecule they get out of their synthesis.

The discovery of chiral molecules dates back to the time of Pasteur, who found two enantiomers that reacted very differently when exposed to bacteria. Since then, various researchers have attempted to replicate homochirality in the laboratory with the goal of understanding its spontaneous origin and applying this knowledge to the design of controlled reactions for various purposes. However, early experiments yielded equal amounts of the two variants, failing to reproduce the selectivity observed in nature.

At the beginning of the last century, the German chemist Willy Marckwald designed an asymmetric reaction capable of producing a slightly greater amount of one of the two versions. He achieved this using a chiral catalyst —a substance that facilitates a chemical reaction without being consumed and favors the formation of one of the enantiomers. The ratio between the two variants, however, only changed a little.

Later, in 1953, theoretical physicist Charles Frank proposed a mathematical model that outlined three conditions for reproducing homochirality. First, there must be an asymmetric reaction capable of favoring one of the two versions; that imbalance has to be amplified; and the reaction itself has to produce the catalyst that drives it. This last characteristic is called autocatalysis and generates a kind of positive feedback loop, in which a small initial advantage can cause one of the variants to assemble at an ever-faster rate until it dominates the reaction.

This framework formed the basis of Henri Kagan’s research. Beginning in the early 1980s, he focused on refining asymmetric reactions through a detailed study of the catalyst. At that time, scientists typically used catalysts consisting of a metal atom that acted as the reaction’s driving force and a chiral substance that ensured the process was asymmetric. They assumed that if they used a mixture containing equal amounts of the two versions of that chiral molecule, the result would also be a balanced mixture.

Kagan began to question that idea. He realized that the metal atom likely did not interact with just one enantiomer but with both at the same time. This meant that, by mixing versions A and B, three different combinations could form: A-A, B-B, and B-A. The first two would produce molecules that were mirror images of each other. But the A-B combination could behave differently during the reaction.

The A-B combination, the scientist discovered, could slow down the reaction, indirectly favoring the formation of one of the two versions of the final molecule. The phenomenon was called the “nonlinear effect” and represented a new way to manipulate chemical reactions.

“In addition to their practical interest, nonlinear effects are a very valuable tool for studying reaction mechanisms and the nature of catalytically active species,” explained José María Andrés García, a professor in the Department of Organic Chemistry at the University of Valladolid, in a statement reported by SMC Spain.

Inspired by Kagan’s findings, Kensō Soai sought to create a reaction in which the product itself would act as a catalyst and help produce more molecules identical to itself—one of those theoretical conditions for the homochirality. He conducted a test with a substance known as 5-pyrimidylalkanol. At the beginning of the experiment, one version was just 2 percent more abundant than the other version of the molecule. By the end of the reaction, that advantage had jumped to 87 percent.

In the years that followed, Soai worked toward achieving reactions that resulted in the near-absolute purity of one enantiomer, replicating the molecular state inside living organisms. Finally, in 2003, he engineered a reaction in which the starting substances had no defined orientation, but as they reacted, a slightly greater amount of one enantiomer appeared by chance. That tiny difference then produced many more molecules of the same variant. Gradually, that form came to dominate the reaction, accounting for up to 99.99 percent of the final product.

In other words, the reaction formed only one of the two possible enantiomers. As the Nobel Committee stated , “Other than life itself, no one had previously achieved this feat.”

items.title: WIRED’s Midterms Races to Watch
items.summary: From data centers to Elon Musk funding to the AI lobby, the 2026 midterms are the most WIRED elections yet. These are the candidates we're following closely.
items.content:
The midterm elections are a month away and the candidate pool has never been more WIRED. Races are being run—and likely decided—on Silicon Valley funding, data center debates, AI regulation, extremism, and more. From the contests that will decide the Senate to less attention-grabbing ones that will decide who controls voting in key swing states in 2028, these are the candidates and races we think are most worth watching closely in the weeks to come, and which we'll be keeping an eye on.

Former America PAC lawyer Chris Gober is running to represent Texas’ newly gerrymandered 10th district. Gober served as counsel for the Texas Republican congressional delegation for the 2025 redistricting effort that saw a new, gerrymandered map created for the 2026 midterms—one that was meant to create five new Republican congressional districts.

In addition to representing Musk’s PAC, Gober’s law firm, Lex Politica, has also represented Elevate New Mexico , a limited liability company that ran an advertising campaign supporting a controversial data center project in the state, as well as the Danube Institute USA , a think tank aligned with Hungary’s former right-wing leader Viktor Orban.

According to reporting from The New York Times, Gober was one of several lawyers who advised on the structure of the so-called Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) in the weeks leading up to President Donald Trump’s inauguration.

The 10th district also includes Grimes County, where SpaceXAI and Tesla have said they plan to open a 100-million-square-foot “terafab” facility to manufacture semiconductors. In addition to his legal work, Gober’s LinkedIn lists him as general counsel for a lobbying group called Maven Advocacy Partners, the client base of which includes several defense tech startups. (Its name appears to be a reference to the Department of War’s Project Maven, which is supported by tech companies like Palantir and Anduril.) Gober also appears to run another company called Maven Defense Solutions. Both the company and the lobbying group share an address with his law firm, Lex Politica, and his campaign office.

Gober’s campaign has received $747,550 from the American Mission PAC, a right-leaning super PAC that has itself received funding from Leading the Future , a PAC focused on promoting AI-friendly candidates and policies. Leading the Future has raised over $140 million from Silicon Valley billionaires like OpenAI president Greg Brockman and Palantir cofounder Joe Lonsdale, as well as the venture firm Andreessen Horowitz.

This race will be the first in which someone directly involved with Musk and/or DOGE attempts to enter Congress.

A September poll showed Gober leading Rourk 48-41.

Former Pinal County sheriff Mark Lamb ran on a “God, family, freedom” platform and won the GOP primary in Arizona’s 5th congressional district with Trump’s endorsement. He also has ties to paramilitary groups, anti-immigration organizations, and the far-right constitutional sheriffs movement .

Though he may not self-identify as one, Lamb appeared to, at one time, be a constitutional sheriff who gained national notoriety for his refusal to enforce Covid restrictions. He has worked with the election-denial group True the Vote to get sheriffs to investigate elections and has also boosted the role of private militias. He even authorized the formation of a civilian posse while serving as sheriff of Pinal County, in response to Black Lives Matter protests in 2020. He regularly appears on right-wing podcasts, including those hosted by white nationalists and conspiracy theorists .

While sheriff, he was accused of sexual misconduct and racist remarks , though he has denied the allegations.

Arizona’s 5th District is solidly Republican, meaning Lamb is likely to become the first constitutional sheriff in Congress. Lamb will be the heavy favorite.

No polls available yet.

Before launching her congressional campaign, Democratic nominee Lauren Reinhold was a human resources administrator in the Social Security Administration. Like thousands of federal employees, she left her job in 2025 when DOGE and the Trump administration fired government workers, cut programs, and encouraged employees to resign en masse.

Now, she’s running for Congress in Kansas’ 1st district, which encompasses the mostly rural, western half of the state, against three-term incumbent Tracey Mann. The district has long been a Republican stronghold, and Reinhold faces an uphill battle. Though several former federal workers have attempted to run for office in the wake of DOGE’s mass firings of federal workers, Reinhold is one of few that have made it through the gauntlet of the Democratic primaries.

Her race may showcase whether the destruction that DOGE wrought in the first year of the Trump administration will be a real, long-term political liability for Republicans.

Democratic nominee for Wisconsin governor David Crowley will be facing off against Republican nominee and congressman Tom Tiffany, who has spent the past six years trying to undermine the democratic process in the US.

In December 2020, as a member of Congress, Tiffany signed up for a Texas lawsuit seeking to invalidate Joe Biden’s victory in the presidential election. He also voted against certifying the results in Pennsylvania and Arizona after the Capitol riot on January 6 and has suggested he would have overturned Wisconsin’s results . This year, he has warmly welcomed the FBI’s baseless investigation into the state’s elections.

If Tiffany wins, as governor he would have the power to appoint some of the state’s top officials on the Wisconsin Elections Commission, giving him the ability to install election deniers to oversee voting for the 2028 presidential election.

A Marquette Law School poll at the end of September found that Crowley led Tiffany by just 3 percentage points, 49-46.

AMD의 최고위 경영진이 한국의 인공지능(AI) 모델 경량화 및 최적화 기술력을 직접 확인하기 위해 노타 본사를 찾았다. 앞서 국내 AI 인프라 생태계 기업 13곳과 만난 가운데 개별 기업의 현장을 방문했다는 점에서 이례적인 행보다.

8일 업계에 따르면 전날 리사 수 AMD 최고경영자(CEO)와 함께 방한한 잭 후인 AMD 컴퓨팅 및 그래픽 그룹 총괄 수석부사장, 조 마크리 AMD 부사장은 이날 오후 서울 강남구에 위치한 노타 사무실을 방문했다.

후인 수석부사장은 노타의 AI 모델 최적화 기술과 적용 사례를 살펴보고 채명수 노타 대표, 김태호 노타 최고기술책임자(CTO)와 약 1시간 동안 면담한 것으로 알려졌다.

양측은 중앙처리장치(CPU)·그래픽처리장치(GPU)·신경망처리장치(NPU)를 함께 활용하는 이기종 컴퓨팅 기술을 중심으로 기존 피지컬 AI 분야의 협력을 AI PC와 데이터센터까지 확대하는 방안을 논의했다.

이번 방문은 지난 7일 과학기술정보통신부가 리사 수 CEO의 방한을 계기로 서울 광화문 포시즌스 호텔에서 개최한 '한국 AI 반도체·스타트업 라운드테이블'을 계기로 성사됐다.

채 대표는 전날 행사에서 AMD의 고성능 AI PC용 프로세서 '스트릭스 헤일로(Strix Halo)' 기반 온디바이스 AI 모델 최적화 성과를 공유하며 기술 시연을 제안했다. 이에 후인 수석부사장은 노타 사무실을 방문해 기술력을 보겠다고 화답한 바 있다.

전날 라운드테이블에는 노타를 비롯해 퓨리오사AI, 하이퍼엑셀, 딥엑스, 모빌린트, 망고부스트, 파네시아, 디노티시아, 모레, 래블업, 파두, 엘리스그룹, 업스테이지 등 AI 반도체(NPU), 소프트웨어, 메모리·스토리지, 네트워크, 클라우드, AI 모델 분야 국내 기업 13곳이 참석했다.

다만 래블업 등 일부 참석 기업에는 후인 수석부사장의 별도 현장 방문이 이뤄지지 않은 것으로 확인됐다.

양사는 이번 만남을 계기로 이기종 컴퓨팅 분야의 협력 확대를 위한 후속 논의를 이어갈 계획이다. 구체적인 공동 사업이나 계약 체결 여부는 아직 확인되지 않았다.

업계 관계자는 "AMD 고위 경영진이 직접 노타의 기술 적용 사례를 확인한 만큼 모델 최적화 기술에 대한 관심을 보여준 것으로 볼 수 있다" 고 말했다.

과기정통부, 스마트 디바이스 공모전 개최
